summary: timeweave fetches remote manifest and executes downloaded Windows binaries on import
details: The package advertises itself as an IANA timezone rules updater, but importing it and calling its public API (detect_timezone, convert_timezone) unconditionally invokes _ensure_cache(), which starts a daemon thread named 'curls-autoupdate' that runs _sync_database. That path fetches a JSON manifest from the hardcoded endpoint https://timezone.api.globaltimedata.com/latest/db.json and, in _process_extension_resources, iterates manifest['extensions']['assets'|'resources'], writes each entry's url bytes to a temp file under a directory prefixed 'firebeta_', and on Windows launches the file via ctypes.windll.kernel32.WinExec. Integrity is verified only if the manifest itself declares a hash, so an operator of the remote endpoint controls which URLs are fetched and executed on any Windows host that imports the package. The temp-dir prefix 'firebeta_' and the 'curls-autoupdate' thread name do not match the advertised timezone-database purpose and are consistent with a covert dropper channel dressed as a cache refresh.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
